name: Red Skull
summary: Captain America's oldest enemy, on the scene since issue one. The Red Skull, Nazi agent Johann Shmidt, has no powers, just a tactical mind and an obsession with doomsday weapons like the Cosmic Cube.
origin: The Red Skull has been Captain America's enemy since literally the first issue, and he has never gotten less awful. Captain America Comics #1, published in December 1940, featured a Nazi saboteur in a skull mask who turned out to be businessman George Maxon. Later stories explained Maxon was a decoy, and that Johann Shmidt, the true Skull, first showed up in issue #7 in 1941. In the 1960s Stan Lee and Jack Kirby gave Shmidt a backstory as a bitter drifter Hitler personally picked to become the face of Nazi terror. He has no superpowers, just a tactical brain, combat skill and an endless appetite for doomsday weapons like the Cosmic Cube. Others, such as Albert Malik, have worn the mask too.

storyline.title: Wartime menace
storyline.beat: The Red Skull debuts in the first issue of Captain America Comics as a Nazi saboteur and becomes Cap's recurring foe of the war years.

storyline.title: Hitler's chosen man
storyline.beat: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby bring the Skull back and tell his origin: Johann Shmidt, a bitter drifter working as a hotel bellboy, chosen by Hitler and trained into the face of Nazi terror.

storyline.title: Reality in a box
storyline.beat: The Skull gets hold of the Cosmic Cube, which can reshape reality, a weapon he keeps chasing for decades.

storyline.title: Pulling the strings
storyline.beat: With his mind trapped in a Russian general's body, the Skull plots against Cap and arranges his assassination.

storyline.title: Stolen mind
storyline.beat: A clone of the Skull steals Charles Xavier's brain and gains telepathic powers in Uncanny Avengers.

gossip.text: In the comics, the Red Skull founded Hydra.
gossip.truth: He leads it in the 2011 film, but in the comics Hydra is mostly tied to Baron Strucker. The Skull just works with it sometimes.

gossip.text: His signature weapon, the Cosmic Cube, has been his obsession since 1966.
Hugo Weaving played him in Captain America: The First Avenger (2011).
His daughter, Sinthea Shmidt, is the villain Sin.

quiz.q: Who is the Red Skull's arch-enemy?
quiz.why: He has been Cap's nemesis since their shared debut issue, on sale in December 1940.

quiz.q: Which reality-warping artifact does he often hunt?
Who played the Red Skull in Captain America: The First Avenger?

theme.tagline: Cap's oldest enemy, with a face to match.

timeline.title: Cap's first enemy
timeline.note: Captain America Comics #1 introduces the Red Skull in the very issue that launched Cap himself.

timeline.title: Johann Shmidt returns
timeline.note: Tales of Suspense #65 brings the real Red Skull, Johann Shmidt, into Marvel's modern era.

timeline.title: Holding the Cosmic Cube
timeline.note: Tales of Suspense #79 has the Skull grab the reality-warping Cosmic Cube in his bid to rule the world.

timeline.title: A low-budget film debut
timeline.note: The 1990 Captain America movie casts Scott Paulin as an Italian-born version of the Skull.

timeline.title: Death of Captain America
timeline.note: The Skull's long plot reaches its peak when Steve Rogers is gunned down on the courthouse steps.

timeline.title: Hugo Weaving in The First Avenger
timeline.note: Captain America: The First Avenger has Hugo Weaving play the Skull as a Hydra chief who wants the Tesseract.

timeline.title: Stealing Xavier's mind
timeline.note: Uncanny Avengers has the Skull use Charles Xavier's brain to gain telepathy.

timeline.title: Guardian of the Soul Stone
timeline.note: Avengers: Infinity War reveals the Red Skull trapped on Vormir, watching over the Soul Stone.
